title: Point guard showdown in Indy ends in Caitlin Clark’s favor: Fever-Wings takeaways
content:
INDIANAPOLIS — As point guard phenoms on the court and the league’s most recognizable names off it, Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers dueled for just the third time in their WNBA careers Friday. The pair of No. 1 picks gave the fans at Gainbridge Fieldhouse their money’s worth.

Clark steered her Indiana Fever to a 98-87 victory with 29 points, 10 assists and three rebounds, while Bueckers carried the Dallas Wings with 29 points, six assists and six rebounds.

Indiana (22-12) has won three straight games and eight of its last 10. Dallas (20-15), meanwhile, has lost six of its last eight.

Clark and Bueckers put on a show in the third quarter, helping their teams emerge from a sluggish first half. Bueckers erupted for 13 points in the frame, tied for the most she’s scored in any quarter this season. The two-time All-Star shot 4 of 6 from the field and drilled two 3s.

Not to be outdone, Clark exploded for 17 points in the period, tying the most points she’s notched in any quarter of her career on 7-of-9 shooting from the field. Earlier this season, when Clark scored 17 points in the fourth quarter of an eventual overtime loss to the Washington Mystics, she drilled five 3s. This time around, Clark used the gravity of her outside shooting to blow by the Wings’ overzealous perimeter defenders for several easy shots in the paint.

Clark briefly exited the game with 40.4 seconds remaining in the half, appearing to tweak her left ankle after accidentally stepping on the foot of Wings forward Alysha Clark.

Clark immediately started limping and grimaced as she was subbed out. The three-time All-Star gingerly walked past her team’s bench and straight to the locker room. However, she started the second half and showed no signs of her injury scare.

With only 13 appearances last season, Clark’s playing time was severely limited due to a slew of injuries. She has been much healthier this season, appearing in 30 of 34 games despite managing a season-long back injury.

Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell scored 8 of her 23 points in the fourth quarter to extend her WNBA single-season record to 18 straight games with at least 20 points. Mitchell was stuck at 19 points late in the fourth quarter before Clark connected with her on a backdoor pass for a layup to keep her streak alive.

Mitchell is now two games shy of tying the WNBA record of 20 straight 20-point games, currently held by Las Vegas Aces superstar and four-time league MVP A’ja Wilson. Wilson set the record across the 2023 and 2024 seasons.

The first hurdle for Bueckers on Friday was navigating the two sides of an arena tunnel, both sides screaming her name, begging for autographs and getting so feisty that a security guard yelled at everyone to calm down. The second was navigating a WNBA game with a lineup besieged by injury. Somehow, this seemed like the easier part.

The burden on the team’s franchise player has reached an absurd level, with Azzi Fudd (knee) and Jessica Shepard (ankle) idled and backup guard Aziaha James (lower leg) out for a significant period. No one is denying it: Bueckers has to figure out how to do more, without doing too much.

“Nobody’s going to replace the people who are out, but it’s on everybody to step up and do a little bit extra,” Bueckers said shortly after passing through the autograph gauntlet. “(It’s) kind of just reading the game, knowing I’ll probably have to be a little bit more aggressive, and just take what the defense gives me.

“That’s a lot of points left on the bench, that’s a lot of shots left on the bench, a lot of production.”

The wait for the cavalry seems likely to persist through the weekend and a trip out to Golden State. Fudd essentially went through a full pregame prep before the doors opened at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. She looked entirely healthy, moving at full speed.

Wings coach Jose Fernandez said Fudd is probably ahead of the others on the comeback trail.

Shepard, an All-Star Game starter averaging 14.2 points, 11.4 rebounds and 5.2 assists per game, was also moving fine in a brief glimpse at the end of Dallas’ shootaround earlier Friday. But Fernandez cautioned Shepard hadn’t done any live work to test the ankle yet.

The best bet, or at least the hope? The Wings get both back — for sure Fudd — for a four-game homestand that runs into the FIBA World Cup break.

“That’s three pieces we need,” Bueckers said of the injured trio. “But we believe in the people in the locker room and believe in what we have, and we take that approach.”

Brian Hamilton contributed to this report.
